key_insight: LLM agents can act as a natural-language home energy scheduler, translating household preferences into near-optimal appliance plans and capturing almost all of the savings found by MILP optimization.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical interface layer for residential demand response and solar-aware load shifting, reducing the usability barrier to advanced HEMS deployment.
method: Tool-calling ReAct agent with native function calling
Uses live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth
evidence_signal: Across tariff, constraint-conflict, solar-co-optimization, and week-long tests, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Reliability drops sharply when actions are text-parsed instead of function-called, so deployment depends on robust tool interfaces and constraint handling.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
